brief.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix rebound 27%/30% on hyperscaler capex relief; HBM4 yield at HBM3E parity, CoWoS gap closing
brief.summary: <cite index="37-8,37-9">SK Hynix closed nearly 30% higher and Samsung closed nearly 27% higher on July 31, marking record single-day gains</cite> after <cite index="37-7">blockbuster earnings from Amazon and Microsoft revived optimism around artificial intelligence spending</cite>. <cite index="5-4">SK Hynix stated HBM4 mass production yield and quality are showing levels close to HBM3E, which has already entered a mature stage</cite>, with <cite index="5-3">mass-production supply to major customers starting in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="44-13">Microsoft guided calendar-2026 capex to roughly $175B, Meta raised FY2026 range to $130–145B, and Alphabet guided $195–205B</cite>, validating sustained HBM/server DRAM demand through 2027. <cite index="26-11">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from around 20% currently to about 10% by end-2026</cite>, easing the packaging bottleneck.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral-to-slight-SKH-overweight. SK Hynix demonstrated execution advantage: <cite index="5-4,5-5">HBM4 yield near HBM3E parity and stable capacity ramp</cite>, plus <cite index="7-1">Goldman/UBS confirm SK maintaining >50% HBM market share through at least 2026</cite>. Samsung improving but still in catch-up: <cite index="2-5">HBM4 samples shipped to NVIDIA and cleared PRA</cite>, yet no equivalent yield disclosure. Both benefit from <cite index="13-1,13-2">Q3 DRAM contract pricing +13–18% QoQ and NAND +10–15% QoQ per TrendForce</cite>. Technical setup: after 27%/30% rally, wait for profit-taking before adding; <cite index="39-11,39-12,39-13">positioning extremely bearish pre-rally, foreign buying continuation key to durable recovery</cite>.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="8-1">Conventional DRAM contract prices projected to rise 13–18% QoQ in Q3 2026, NAND 10–15%</cite>, down from <cite index="12-7,12-8">Q2's 58–63% DRAM and 70–75% NAND QoQ increases</cite>, signaling deceleration. <cite index="8-9,8-10">AI inference and hyperscale demand keeps DRAM/NAND supply constrained; manufacturers shift capacity to higher-margin server products, leaving less for consumer</cite>. <cite index="10-5,10-6,10-7">Samsung and SK Hynix control ~70% DRAM, signaled no aggressive capacity expansion; analysts project memory price rally extending past 2028</cite>. HBM remains the safety valve: <cite index="3-1">HBM3E expected to account for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026, HBM4 gradually gaining traction</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-3,5-4">SK Hynix began HBM4 mass-production supply in Q2 2026, with yield and quality near mature HBM3E levels</cite>. <cite index="2-5,2-6">Samsung shipped HBM4 samples to NVIDIA, exceeding 11 Gbps per pin requirement for Rubin platform</cite>. <cite index="1-2,1-6">Both suppliers prioritizing HBM4 ramp; HBM3E supply remains tight and lags demand</cite>. <cite index="1-5">H200 export approval to China drove HBM3E demand above expectations (six stacks per H200)</cite>. Pricing: <cite index="1-2,1-4">Industry expects ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026; ongoing AI accelerator launches by global big tech keep demand on steady growth path</cite>. Next-gen: <cite index="4-8,4-9">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples reaching 16Gbps per pin, >20% power efficiency gain</cite>; <cite index="5-6">HBM4E mass production targeted for 2027</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix +30%, Samsung +27% on record single-day gains
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="37-7">Amazon/Microsoft earnings revived AI spending optimism</cite>; <cite index="39-8">SK Group Chairman disclosed SK Hynix share purchases, bolstering confidence</cite>. Reversal from <cite index="38-2,38-3">July 29's -14.7% SKH / -13.4% Samsung selloff</cite>. Near-term: <cite index="39-10,39-11">gains of this magnitude unlikely to continue, but rebound has room as positioning was extremely bearish</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guides sum to ~$690–725B, up 77% YoY
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="44-13">Microsoft $175B, Meta $130–145B, Alphabet $195–205B</cite>; <cite index="47-1">Amazon hiked 2026 capex to $220B</cite>. <cite index="44-11">Market rewarded Microsoft/Amazon (Azure +43% YoY, AWS +37% YoY) with metered cloud revenue; punished Meta/Apple lacking external line</cite>. Memory implication: sustained orders for HBM, server DRAM/NAND through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix HBM4 yield nears HBM3E, mass production began Q2 2026
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="5-4,5-5">Yield at HBM3E parity, stably increasing production capacity</cite>. Unveiled <cite index="5-8,5-9">iHBM cooling tech cutting thermal resistance by 30% via hybrid bonding</cite>. Credibility gap vs. Samsung narrows but SK retains time-to-market lead.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung cleared HBM4 PRA, samples to NVIDIA exceed 11Gbps spec
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="2-3,2-5,2-6">Cleared Production Readiness Approval; samples shipped to NVIDIA for Rubin, already exceeded 11 Gbps per pin</cite>. <cite index="2-7">Using 1c-class DRAM + 4nm logic base die</cite>. Volume production contingent on NVIDIA sign-off; <cite index="2-8">manufacturing lines already prepared</cite>. Faster catch-up than street expected.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM +13–18% QoQ Q3, NAND +10–15%: pricing rally decelerating
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="13-1,13-2">Contract pricing still rising but at slower pace than Q2's 58–63% DRAM / 70–75% NAND</cite>. <cite index="8-2,8-9">Long-term server deals capping server DRAM prices; AI inference/hyperscale demand keeps supply constrained</cite>. Consumer: <cite index="8-4,8-5">Higher memory costs feeding into retail, weighing on PC/smartphone shipments</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="26-2,26-11">TSMC monthly CoWoS capacity reaching 120–140K wafers in 2026; supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by year-end</cite>. <cite index="26-4">Severe 2.5D packaging shortage to moderate by 2027, CoWoS capacity expanding >60% by 2027</cite>. Eases key bottleneck for Blackwell/Rubin GPU shipments; direct uplift for Samsung/SKH HBM attachment rates.

news_pulse.headline: HBM3E pricing up ~20% in 2026; H200 China exports drive demand
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="1-5">NVIDIA H200 export approval to China drove HBM3E demand above expectations (six HBM3E stacks per H200)</cite>. <cite index="1-4">Ongoing AI accelerator launches keep HBM3E demand on steady growth path despite HBM4 entry</cite>. <cite index="1-7">2026 HBM revenue mix: ~55% HBM4, 45% HBM3E; HBM4 to rapidly absorb demand from Q3</cite>. Pricing power intact through H1 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Capex scrutiny rising: Oracle CDS tripled since Sept, one hyperscaler may pause
news_pulse.implication: <cite index="22-8">Jim Cramer: one hyperscaler may signal capex freeze or OpenAI credit deterioration</cite>. <cite index="21-7,21-8">Oracle 5-year CDS tripled since September; trading volumes surged above norms</cite>. Tail risk: if hyperscaler pauses, <cite index="22-10">multiple compression cascades fastest at Oracle, then Amazon, then Alphabet</cite>. Memory implication: DRAM/NAND order pushouts in H2, but HBM contracts locked.

brief.derivatives_signal: No derivatives payload provided. Infer from cash: <cite index="39-3">KOSPI surged 14% on July 31, on track for largest one-day jump</cite>. <cite index="39-9">Short-covering and leveraged ETF rebalancing amplified gains</cite>. Near-term skew: realized vol collapse post-squeeze creates asymmetric put-selling opportunity if foreign flows continue; <cite index="39-12,39-13">real test is whether foreign buying continues after short-covering fades</cite>. Watch KOSPI 200 futures premium normalization and ADR basis vs. local close.
